text: A man who does not solidly establish, and really deserve, a character of truth, probity, good manners, and good morals, at his first setting out in the world, may impose, and shine like a meteor for a very short time, but will very soon vanish, and be extinguished with contempt.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXIII, to his son, London, May 17, Old Style 1750
